content: The Bixby Center for Global Reproductive Health and Policy at the University of California, San Francisco, is based in San Francisco, California. Dr. Rintaro Mori serves as the Director of the Department of Health Policy at the National Research Institute for Child Health and Development in Tokyo, Japan. Professor James Neilson, who chaired the May 2017 consultation, is the Coordinating Editor of the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group and a professor at the University of Liverpool in the United Kingdom. Hiromi Obara is a Health Policy Advisor for the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) in Vientiane, Lao People’s Democratic Republic. Professor Oladapo Olayemi is the Head of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan, Nigeria. Professor Robert Pattinson is the Director of the South African Medical Research Council/University of Pretoria Maternal and Infant Health Care Strategies Unit at Kalafong Hospital in Pretoria, South Africa. Dr. Harshad Sanghvi is the Chief Medical Officer at Jhpiego, an affiliate of Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland, USA. Dr. Mandisa Singata-Madliki is the Deputy Director of the Effective Care Research Unit at East London Hospital Complex, University of Fort Hare, South Africa. Professor Jorge E. Tolosa is a Coordinator for the Global Network for Perinatal and Reproductive Health (GNPRH) and a professor in the Division of Maternal-Fetal Medicine at Oregon Health & Science University in Portland, Oregon, USA, as well as the Department of Gynecology and Obstetrics at Universidad de Antioquia in Medellín, Colombia. Professor Hayfaa Wahabi is the Chair of Evidence-Based Healthcare and Knowledge Translation at King Saud University in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The External Review Group includes Blami Dao, Technical Director for Western and Central Africa at Jhpiego, and Professor G. Justus Hofmeyr, who is affiliated with the Effective Care Research Unit at the Universities of Witwatersrand and Fort Hare in South Africa. Professor Caroline Homer is the Director of the Centre for Midwifery, Child, and Family Health at the University of Technology Sydney, Australia. Professor Vanora Hundley is based at Bournemouth University in the United Kingdom, specializing in midwifery and maternal health. Barbara Levy is the Vice President of Health Policy at the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists in Washington, D.C., USA. Professor Ashraf Nabhan is a faculty member in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Ain Shams University in Cairo, Egypt. The Technical Working Group includes Edgardo Abalos, Vice Director of the Centro Rosarino de Estudios Perinatales in Rosario, Argentina, and Professor Debra Bick, who specializes in evidence-based midwifery practice at King’s College London in the United Kingdom. Meghan Bohren is a consultant in the Department of Reproductive Health and Research at the World Health Organization (WHO) in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Monica Chamillard and Dr. Virginia Diaz are medical doctors at the Centro Rosarino de Estudios Perinatales in Rosario, Argentina. Professor Soo Downe specializes in midwifery studies at the University of Central Lancashire in the United Kingdom. Dr. Therese Dowswell is a Research Associate with the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group at the University of Liverpool, United Kingdom. Kenneth Finlayson is a Senior Research Assistant in Midwifery Studies at the University of Central Lancashire. Frances Kellie is the Managing Editor of the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group at the University of Liverpool. Dr. Theresa Lawrie is a consultant in evidence-based medicine based in Bath, United Kingdom. Dr. Julia Pasquale is a medical doctor at the Centro Rosarino de Estudios Perinatales in Rosario, Argentina. Dr. Elham Shakibazadeh is an Associate Professor in the Department of Health Education and Promotion at Tehran University of Medical Sciences in Iran. Dr. Gill Thomson is an Associate Professor specializing in maternal and infant nutrition at the University of Central Lancashire in the United Kingdom. External partners and observers include Diogo Ayres-de-Campos, a member of the FIGO Committee for Safe Motherhood and Newborn Health, and Petra ten Hoope-Bender, a Technical Advisor for Sexual and Reproductive Health at the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA). Mechthild M. Gross, Head of the Midwifery Research and Education Unit at Hannover Medical School in Germany, represents the International Confederation of Midwives (ICM). Mary Ellen Stanton is a Senior Reproductive Health Advisor at the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in Washington, D.C., USA. Alison Wright is the Vice President for UK and Global Membership at the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists in London, United Kingdom. WHO regional office representatives include Léopold Ouedraogo, Regional Advisor for Reproductive Health in the African Region; Bremen De Mucio, Regional Advisor for Sexual and Reproductive Health in the Americas; Karima Gholbzouri, Medical Officer for Reproductive and Maternal Health in the Eastern Mediterranean Region; Mavjuda Babamuradova, Medical Officer for Sexual and Reproductive Health in the European Region; and Mari Nagai, Technical Officer for Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health in the Western Pacific Region. The guideline development process involved experts such as Professor Hany Abdel-Aleem, Dr. Fernando Althabe, Dr. Melania Maria Ramos de Amorim, Professor Michel Boulvain, Dr. Aparajita Gogoi, Professor Tina Lavender, Professor Pisake Lumbiganon, Ms. Silke Mader, Professor Suellen Miller, Dr. Rintaro Mori, Professor James Neilson, Dr. Hiromi Obara, Professor Oladapo Olayemi, Professor Robert Pattinson, Dr. Harshad Sanghvi, Dr. Mandisa Singata-Madliki, and others. These experts contributed their knowledge in obstetrics, midwifery, maternal and child health, and systematic review methodologies. The guidelines emphasize respectful maternity care (RMC), effective communication, companionship during labor, and evidence-based practices for labor and childbirth. Effective communication training should be integrated into professional education, and culturally appropriate materials should be made available. Evidence-based practices, such as intermittent fetal heart rate auscultation and appropriate use of pain relief methods, should guide clinical management.
